body.statement: Under the regular random-design law and conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, averaging the conditional frontier over \((X_{st})\) gives \[\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]\asymp R_{\star}.\] The \(N^{-\kappa}\) converse, and therefore the four-channel equivalence, is conditional on that maintained direction. Thus the oracle region is \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{or}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{or}}=o(N^{-\kappa})\), and their boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\kappa}\), where \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is the maximum of the treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and spacing terms. For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the rate reduces to \(n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}\vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}\) when \(0<\lambda\le1\).
body.justification: The result turns the realized-geometry theorem into an explicit phase diagram and discharges the scalar early-kill test without a pointwise logarithm.
body.gap: Stone (1982) gives the ordinary \(d\)-dimensional smoothing exponent and Gaiffas (2007) gives a spatially normalized global sup-risk with a logarithm; neither separates replication saturation, pointwise spacing, and an external donor modulus.
body.consumer: Power calculations for event studies can trade additional donors, longer pre-event histories, and more within-cohort replication on a common risk scale.
